preconditions.description: t is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive, representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and q == int(q) and 2 <= n <= 100 and 1 <= q <= 100 for n, q in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line))
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer between 2 and 100 inclusive (length of string s), and q is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive (number of queries).

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for s, n in zip((line for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::] if line.strip() and not ' ' in line), (int(n) for n, q in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line))))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the string s has length exactly n and consists only of characters '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: all(l_i == int(l_i) and r_i == int(r_i) and 1 <= l_i < r_i <= n for l_i, r_i in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line))
preconditions.description: For each query, l_i and r_i are integers such that 1 ≤ l_i < r_i ≤ n, where n is the length of the string s for the current test case.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip() in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines() if stdout_line.strip())
postconditions.description: For each query, the output is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive).

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line.strip() == 'YES') == any(all(s[i] == s[l_i + k - 1] for k in range(1, len(substr) + 1)) and len(subseq_indices) >= 2 and not any(subseq_indices[j] == subseq_indices[j + 1] - 1 for j in range(len(subseq_indices) - 1)) for subseq_indices in combinations(range(1, n + 1), len(substr)) if all(s[i] == s[l_i + k - 1] for k, i in enumerate(subseq_indices, 1))) for (l_i, r_i), substr, stdout_line in zip((line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line), (s[l_i - 1:r_i] for s, l_i, r_i in zip((line for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::] if line.strip() and not ' ' in line), (int(l_i) for l_i, r_i in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line)), (int(r_i) for l_i, r_i in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::] if line.strip() and ' ' in line)))), stdout.splitlines() if stdout_line.strip()))
postconditions.description: For each query (l_i, r_i), the output is 'YES' if and only if there exists a good subsequence in s that matches the substring s[l_i...r_i]. A good subsequence is defined as a subsequence of length ≥ 2 that is not contiguous (no two indices in the subsequence are consecutive).
